audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor contains hedge benefits that expired immediately afterward
audit_findings.magnitude: H1 2026 interest expense was $28.2m, $7.7m higher year over year and equal to 7.3% of the $105.8m anchor; replacement swaps cover $425.0m at 3.280% versus the expired $500.0m swaps at 0.370%
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest expense remains in equity-level OE, so a higher recurring borrowing cost directly reduces the anchor and every projected cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to December 31, 2025, our interest rate swaps matured, increasing our exposure to interest rate variability.
audit_findings.explanation: The favorable FY2025 swaps' expiration is demonstrated, as is a material subsequent increase in interest expense. The latest 10-Q shows replacement hedges, so the company is not wholly unhedged, but they cover less principal at a substantially higher fixed rate. The exact sustainable annual reduction remains unresolved because the record does not isolate hedge expiry, the revolver's full-year cost, and other interest movements.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild annual interest expense using the June 2026 debt balances, SOFR margins, $425.0m replacement swaps, unhedged floating debt, and a full year on the $100.0m revolver; rerun all scenarios with normalized after-tax OE.

audit_findings.title: A $2.7 billion TRA claim is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest TRA liability $2,726.4m, equal to 167% of the $1,637.0m base equity value; filed TRA payments were $23.6m in 2025 and $94.0m in 2024
audit_findings.mechanism: TRA cash payments are financing outflows ahead of common equity; they must be captured either in OE through a reconciled cash-tax treatment or as a net claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had a liability of $ 2,731.9 million related to its projected obligations under the Tax Receivable Agreements in connection with the Reorganization Transactions and units of ZoomInfo Holdings LLC.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and its absence from the bridge are demonstrated. Whether its economic burden was already captured in OE is unresolved because the supplied valuation does not reconcile GAAP tax expense, deferred-tax additions, cash taxes, tax benefits, and TRA payments. The gross liability must not simply be deducted because it accompanies tax attributes and deferred-tax assets, but omission of the net cash burden is plainly capable of reversing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Produce a year-by-year tax schedule reconciling GAAP tax expense, deferred taxes, cash taxes, realized tax savings, and TRA payments; value only the uncaptured net burden and rerun the bridge and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized SBC may bypass the no-add-back rail
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.2m in FY2025; 5.9% of the anchor and, if entirely omitted and recurring, approximately $0.20-$0.29 per share across the scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized SBC can escape both current compensation expense and a cash-only capex deduction while its later amortization may be added back, overstating OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Qualifying internal use software costs incurred during the application development stage, which consist primarily of internal product development costs, outside services, personnel costs (including equity-based compensation), and purchased software license costs, are capitalized and amortized over the estimated useful life of the asset.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the $6.2m was omitted is unresolved. Even assuming complete omission and treating it as recurring, the computed base-value reduction is about $87m or $0.26 per share, leaving base value near $4.68 versus the $4.13 price and reducing buy-below only to about $3.27, still below the price. It therefore does not independently change the stated valuation decision.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $6.2m through the FY2025 OE worksheet, deduct it once if absent, and ensure subsequent software amortization does not reverse the compensation charge.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a non-operating TRA remeasurement gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.9m pre-tax; 6.5% of the anchor and, before any tax adjustment, approximately $0.22-$0.33 per share across the scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: A noncash, nonrecurring TRA remeasurement gain would inflate the OE anchor and all projected cash flows if retained.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we recognized a TRA remeasurement gain of $ 6.9 million principally due to a revaluation for the blended state tax rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The gain is demonstrated, but its inclusion in OE is unresolved. Even assuming the entire pre-tax gain remained in the anchor, the computed base-value reduction is about $97m or $0.29 per share, leaving base value near $4.65 and buy-below near $3.26. The proper after-tax adjustment would be smaller, so this item does not independently change the buy conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace Other income in the FY2025 OE calculation and remove the $6.9m gain with its specific tax effect if it was retained.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved litigation could create claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Damages, settlements, defense costs, or operating restrictions could reduce future OE or create claims requiring an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on the information known by the Company as of the date of this filing, except where otherwise indicated, it is not possible to provide an estimated amount of any loss or range of loss that may occur with respect to these matters, including without limitation, the matters described below.
audit_findings.explanation: The pending proceedings and absence of an estimable loss range are demonstrated, but no filed amount establishes the potential unreserved exposure. H1 2026 already included $12.2m of litigation settlement expense and $5.7m of related cash payments, while additional securities and derivative actions were filed, but those figures do not quantify the listed claims. Materiality therefore cannot be established or dismissed from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current docket status, class-certification and settlement developments, claimed statutory damages, insurance coverage and limits, accruals, and any injunction exposure; rerun OE or the bridge when a probable or estimable amount emerges.

audit_findings.title: Serial restructuring and lease-exit costs require consistent normalization
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 charges $40.3m and cash payments $15.5m, equal to 38.1% and 14.7% of the $105.8m anchor; H1 2026 charges were $45.3m and cash payments were $30.5m
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring cash restructuring and unavoidable lease payments reduce sustainable OE, while noncash impairment remeasurements may be normalized without removing the underlying cash obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate that restructuring and transaction-related expenses, including potential impairments, will be influenced by activities related to potential future acquisitions, strategic restructuring efforts, and leased spaces that we plan to sublease, which could cause these costs to vary, potentially significantly, from our historic levels.
audit_findings.explanation: Repeated restructuring is demonstrated across 2023-2026, including a new reduction affecting about 20% of headcount. The supplied record does not establish how the OE series separated cash costs from noncash impairments. Given the scale relative to the anchor, stripping all charges could materially overstate value, while retaining every impairment could materially understate it.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each year's restructuring charges to cash severance, transition costs, lease payments, termination payments, impairment and modification gains; establish a consistent recurring cash allowance and rerun the OE history, anchor, and all scenarios.
